CNBC just noted that half of Under Armour's profit is coming from tariff refunds, and that broadly the refunds are propping up corporate profits.

Weird those refunds aren't going to consumers. Also weird prices aren't coming down. Almost as if tariffs don't drive inflation.

congress-legislation.quote:
1. After Abdul El-Sayed's win in Michigan, a DC-based advocacy group Third Way will now spend $15 million to attack 'the left.' They frame themselves as moderate Democrats. Why aren't they that spending money attacking the GOP? 

The answer requires explaining who they are.

There are a few more, but that's the gist. The $15m to attack the left is an attempt to prevent the Democratic Party from taxing capital or preventing mergers or monopolies. It has nothing to do with partisan politics in the way one might imagine. It's political insurance.

Most Americans think of political moderation or centrism as fair and even-keeled. Or at least they have. But 'moderate' or 'centrist,' hijacked by Third Way, means representing the interests of banker-Americans. And if that doesn't change, get ready for a lot more radicalism.
